analysis.title: Globant SA (GLOB): Demand headwinds in Middle East offset underlying progress in AI service initiatives
key_insights: GS expects GLOB to be range bound after a narrowed 2026 outlook. Progress on AI initiatives is offset by incremental demand weakness in the Middle East.
GS says investor expectations were low heading into the quarter because of macro pressure on some verticals and Globant's Middle East exposure.
Globant expects its AI Pods business to reach an exit run rate ARR of $130mn by end of 2026, up from $110mn previously.

GS believes Globant can eventually capitalize on a large pipeline of AI-led project work, but it may take several quarters before its most exposed end markets and clients return to a favorable growth profile.
3Q26 revenue of $611mn was in line with the Street at $613mn and GS at $611mn, down 1.0% Y/Y.
3Q26 non-GAAP gross margin of 36.8% was above GS at 34.0% and in line with the Street at 36.7%. Non-GAAP operating margin of 14.1% was in line with the Street at 14.0% and below GS at 14.7%.
2026 revenue guidance was lowered to $2.429-$2.437bn, from growth of (1.1)%-0.3% Y/Y prior to (1.1)%-(0.7)% Y/Y. GS prior and the Street were at $2.446bn.
2026 adjusted operating margin guidance was maintained at 13.5%-14.5%, against GS at 14.5% and the Street at 13.9%.
2026 adjusted EPS guidance was lowered to $5.77-$5.87 from $5.75-$6.15, against GS prior at $6.00 and the Street at $5.89.
4Q26 revenue guidance of $596-$604mn compares with GS prior at $613mn and the Street at $612mn.
GS sees the results as broadly neutral for its IT Services coverage.
GS cut its 2026 revenue estimate to $2,433mn from $2,446mn, and its 2027 and 2028 estimates by 2.9% and 4.3%.
GS lowered its 12-month price target to $50 from $52, based on a 7X P/E (down from 8X on lower peer multiples) applied to forward 12-month EPS. The rating is Neutral.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $50 from $52 on a lower peer-based P/E multiple of 7X versus 8X. Estimates are essentially unchanged and the stock is expected to be range bound.

sector_views.rationale: GS views Globant's results as broadly neutral for its IT Services coverage.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported revenue $611mn vs Street (Visible Alpha) $613mn and GS est $611mn, -1.0% Y/Y.
3Q26 non-GAAP EPS from continuing operations reported $1.48 vs Street est $1.50 and GS est $1.49.
3Q26 non-GAAP gross margin reported 36.8% vs Street est 36.7% and GS est 34.0%. Non-GAAP operating margin reported 14.1% vs Street est 14.0% and GS est 14.7%.
FY26 company revenue guidance $2.429-$2.437bn (-1.1% to -0.7% Y/Y, includes +0.7% FX), vs GS prior and Street est $2.446bn.
FY26 company adjusted EPS guidance $5.77-$5.87 (from $5.75-$6.15) vs GS prior est $6.00 and Street est $5.89.
4Q26 company revenue guidance $596-$604mn with neutral FX, vs GS prior est $613mn and Street est $612mn.
GS 2026E revenue by vertical: Media and Entertainment $508mn, Travel & Hospitality $294mn (-6.6% Y/Y), Banks, Financial Services and Insurance $493mn, Professional Services $208mn (-11.0% Y/Y).
risk_factors: Upside risks: earlier-than-expected recovery in discretionary spending, increased demand for AI-related projects, stronger-than-expected deal conversion.
Downside risks: demand slowdown in unique verticals such as media, sports and other entertainment, further revenue slowdown, dilutive M&A.
Macro uncertainty pressuring some of Globant's verticals, plus meaningful Middle East exposure.
geopolitical: Demand weakness in the Middle East is cited as a headwind for Globant, which has meaningful exposure to the region.
